picks.title: Audible turns to AI to help users discover audiobooks
picks.excerpt: Audible's new AI-generated audio previews summarize a book's themes and what readers liked about it, in addition to playing the narrated sample.
picks.rationale: New product release: Audible's AI 'Audio Discovery' previews change how listeners find audiobooks, and how authors' books get pitched to them.

picks.title: How I've Used AI to Improve My Writing Business
picks.excerpt: Most discussion of AI in the writing and publishing community has focused on its harms. Jane Friedman details how she has put AI to work in her publishing-industry business.
picks.rationale: The most practical item in the pool: a respected publishing-industry voice lays out the concrete AI uses she relies on in her own writing business.

picks.title: Beyond the Download: What Counts as Scholarly Content Use in the Age of AI?
picks.excerpt: New usage metrics are needed as AI assistants intermediate between researchers and publisher content. What should count, and what can those numbers say about the value of research?
picks.rationale: New argument: download counts stop working once AI assistants sit between researchers and content. This matters for publisher licensing and library renewals.

picks.title: From AI Adoption to AI Practice: Building Governed AI in Scholarly Publishing
picks.excerpt: How a publisher can make AI useful across the organization while keeping control of confidential information, editorial decisions and accountability.
picks.rationale: Actionable operating guide for publishers rolling out governed internal AI (confidentiality, editorial control, accountability). It is distinct from the 10-14 'moving faster than the evidence' post.

dedup.note: The Bookseller 'Publishing Ireland conference' pick was removed after the fact-check pass: the article is paywalled and only a one-line standfirst is reachable, so its AI coverage can't be verified. No replacement was added and the section stays at 4 picks. The two remaining eligible candidates don't qualify. The Guardian 'wild west' feature is a roundup and extra reporting on prize/AI-use scandals already published (Goncourt 11-05, Caine 11-12, Quebec 10-22, French manuscript screening 11-15), so it counts as the same running story with no new event, and it was passed over on 11-16 too. The Lit Hub William Blake essay is opinion with no news hook, so adding it would be padding. Dropped as duplicates / running-story repeats: Good e-Reader Audible Audio Discovery (same launch as the TechCrunch pick; brief caps Audible at 1); Le Monde Pascal Prize (same as the 2026-10-21 Bookseller Prix Pascal card); Futurism Coral Hart AI romance (same running story as the 2026-10-25 Times Now '370 books' card, also dropped 11-16); Scholarly Kitchen IFRRO CEO interview (commentary on the IFRRO study published 2026-10-30, no new release); Book Riot 'Investigations targeting BIPOC authors' (commentary on the French AI-manuscript scandal already covered 11-05/11-15). Excluded by cross-section assignment: Books+Publishing ASA 'Not AI's to Take' (music only) and Voice Over Herald Equity–Pact ballot (movies only). Picks: 3 outlets, max 2 per outlet (Scholarly Kitchen). I could not grep published_urls.json with Read-only tools, so the orchestrator should exact-grep the 4 URLs across all sections before roll.
